pathway.title: AdaptHealth Corp. — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: AdaptHealth earned less per dollar of revenue in 2026 even as revenue grew. Revenue for nine months 2026 was USD 2,165,828 thousand, up 9.72%, but Adjusted EBITDA was USD 378,462 thousand, down 4.23%, and the margin fell by 2.5 points to 17.5%. The decline sits in Sleep Health and Wellness at Home, whose margins fell, while Respiratory Health improved. The mechanism is a rapid ramp of capitated contracts, which carried start-up labour cost and a supplier price increase before volumes settled; margin recovered in each quarter of 2026 but remains below Q3 2025 [Financial base, Business context].

Cash generation is the weakest link. Free cash flow was USD 2,632 thousand for nine months 2026, against USD 140,095 thousand a year earlier, because equipment purchases rose to USD 392,981 thousand to serve capitated members. On a continuing basis Adjusted EBITDA less equipment purchases was negative USD 6,796 thousand, against positive USD 123,716 thousand a year earlier. Acquisitions of USD 127,422 thousand and tax receivable agreement payments of USD 26,846 thousand were funded by borrowing, which is how principal debt rose to USD 1,894,969 thousand from USD 1,750,000 thousand [Financial base].

Leverage has risen in direction but cannot be measured on one perimeter. Trailing Adjusted EBITDA on the current business equals recast FY2025 less USD 16,717 thousand, while debt is higher, so the ratio is higher than at year-end 2025. No recast FY2025 figure exists in the sources. On management guidance, principal debt is 3.66x the midpoint of USD 517.5 million of guided Adjusted EBITDA, an indicative figure that treats a forecast as given [Financial base].

Liquidity and maturities are sound in the near term. Cash was USD 80,687 thousand and undrawn revolver availability USD 268.7 million, for USD 349,387 thousand. Scheduled repayments are USD 4.0 million in the rest of 2026 and USD 16.0 million in 2027. The 6.125% notes were redeemed in August 2026. The 4.625% notes of USD 500.0 million fall due on 2029-08-01 and the 5.125% notes of USD 600.0 million on 2030-03-01, and the USD 794,969 thousand of term loans and revolver spring to about 2029-05-02 if more than USD 150.0 million of the notes remains outstanding then [Financial base].

Interest cover is adequate but lower. Adjusted EBITDA was 3.92x cash interest paid for nine months 2026 against 4.12x for nine months 2025. Covenant tests exist on total leverage and interest coverage, the company reports compliance at 2026-09-30, and the levels are not supplied, so headroom is not measurable [Source readiness, Financial base].

The business is shifting toward at-risk capitated revenue. It was 13.3% of nine-month 2026 revenue against 4.8%, and under these contracts the company bears members' care cost. The counterparty, term and price of the main contract are not disclosed, so concentration cannot be sized. Management claims a sequential improvement in contract profitability in Q3 2026 and offers no contract profit to test it [Business context].

Portfolio change and claims outside debt add outcomes that are not yet resolved. The sale of Diabetes Health for USD 235.0 million in cash is signed but not closed, and use of proceeds is not stated. The eCommerce subsidiary moved into a joint venture for a minority stake. Claims outside the debt figure include the tax receivable agreement liability of USD 238.9 million, operating leases of USD 126,716 thousand, finance leases of USD 39,357 thousand, two federal civil investigative demands, an unquantified cybersecurity incident and a consumer class settlement with USD 14.1 million remaining liability [Financial base, Business context].

runs.text: Strengths. Scale and diversification of referral sources: the company serves about 4.8 million patients a year through about 660 locations in 48 states, with fixed monthly equipment reimbursements and product resupply forming most revenue [Documentary Fact; Business context]. Operating cash flow is large: USD 395,613 thousand for nine months 2026, against USD 418,587 thousand a year earlier, which still funds a substantial equipment programme [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Liquidity and structure: USD 349,387 thousand of liquidity, a revolver running to April 2031 subject to the springing maturity, and no notes due before 2029 [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Shareholder behaviour: no dividends or buybacks, voluntary term loan repayments of USD 218.8 million in 2025, and no controlling sponsor shown among holders near 10% and 8% [Documentary Fact; Business context]. Recovery of margin through 2026: the Adjusted EBITDA margin rose from 15.4% in Q1 2026 (derived) to 17.8% in Q2 and 19.0% in Q3 [Documentary Fact; Financial base].

Weaknesses. Margin and earnings quality: nine-month margin down to 17.5% from 20.0%, with "other non-recurring" add-backs recurring in both years at USD 15,085 thousand and USD 20,439 thousand [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Thin free cash flow after equipment spending, with growth funded by debt [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Rising debt: principal debt up USD 144,969 thousand and net principal debt up USD 170,418 thousand since year-end 2025 [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Cost-of-care risk and concentration in a small set of capitated contracts whose terms are undisclosed [Documentary Fact for the share, Insufficient Information for the terms; Business context]. Goodwill impairments of USD 328,987 thousand in nine months 2026 and a Sleep Health reporting unit within 20% of carrying value, which signal weaker projected cash flows in two reporting units and a risk of more [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Goodwill of USD 2,158,313 thousand is 51.38% of total assets and exceeds total equity, so tangible equity is negative and balance sheet asset quality offers less comfort [Analyst Interpretation; Calculations]. Unquantified claims: investigations, the cybersecurity incident and a supplier bed recall [Documentary Fact; Business context]. Management continuity: a change of Chief Financial Officer between the Q2 and Q3 2026 reports and an unreconciled restructuring savings figure [Documentary Fact; Business context].

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The one transaction that changes the credit is the pending sale of the Diabetes Health business under an asset purchase agreement dated 2026-07-19 between the company and RGH Enterprises, LLC for 235.0 million in cash, subject to customary purchase price adjustments (Q3 10-Q page:27, page:59, page:96). It is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, subject to certain regulatory approvals and customary conditions; the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period has expired. The status is signed and pending, not closed. The business is already reported as discontinued operations, and its goodwill and intangibles are carried as assets held for sale. The filings do not say how the proceeds will be used. The credit agreement requires mandatory prepayments in connection with certain dispositions of assets to the extent proceeds are not reinvested (Q3 10-Q page:41-42), and the notes may require an offer to purchase upon the sale of certain assets (page:42), but whether either applies to this sale is not stated, and the agreement and indentures are not in the sources. Use of proceeds, any price adjustment and any transition services remain Insufficient Information. A second portfolio move, the eCommerce contribution to a joint venture on 2026-07-29, is closed; the company holds a minority interest carried at 42.5 million and the filing says the transaction is not a strategic shift (page:16-17).

On debt, two financings occurred in the year. On 2026-04-10 the company entered the 2026 Credit Agreement, with a 325.0 million term loan, a 325.0 million delayed-draw term loan and 450.0 million of revolving commitments, maturing April 2031 with a springing maturity tied to the 4.625% and 5.125% notes (Q3 10-Q page:40). On 2026-07-27 the delayed-draw term loan was borrowed in full and, with cash on hand, redeemed the 6.125% notes at par on 2026-08-03 (page:40, page:89). No new bond issue is recorded in the sources for 2026. The sale proceeds, if applied to debt, would be a prepayment rather than a new issue. The financing terms, security, guarantors and covenants are described in the financial base handoff and rest on filing summaries because the executed credit agreement and indentures are not supplied. Ratings and market quotes are not supplied.

"Pre-recast" means the FY2025 10-K and the Q1 2026 10-Q, which include Diabetes Health as a fourth segment. Figures from the two perimeters are never placed side by side as like for like. Debt, cash and the lease and TRA liabilities sit at the group level and are not changed by the recast, so they are comparable across dates.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On the perimeter the filings now use, AdaptHealth is growing revenue faster than it is growing earnings. Nine-month 2026 revenue rose 9.72% year on year, but Adjusted EBITDA fell 4.23% and the Adjusted EBITDA margin fell by 2.5 points, to 17.5%. The pressure is concentrated in the Sleep Health and Wellness at Home segments, whose margins fell, while Respiratory Health improved. Management attributes it to the ramp of an exclusive capitated agreement with a national integrated delivery network, a manufacturer price increase and elevated labour, and says contract profitability improved sequentially in Q3 2026. The recast quarterly margin did rise each quarter of 2026, from 15.4% (derived) to 17.8% to 19.0%, but remains below the 21.7% of Q3 2025. Cash generation is the weakest part of the base: operating cash flow was 395,613 thousand for nine months, but equipment purchases of 392,981 thousand absorbed nearly all of it, leaving free cash flow of 2,632 thousand. Debt is higher, with principal of 1,894,969 thousand against 1,750,000 thousand at year-end 2025, while cash is lower at 80,687 thousand. Liquidity is adequate on the filing's numbers, at 349,387 thousand of cash plus undrawn revolver, and the maturity profile improved because the 6.125% notes were redeemed in August 2026 with a delayed-draw term loan. The base has four limits. There is no recast full-year 2025 figure, so a trailing leverage ratio on the current perimeter cannot be computed. The covenant levels and the issuer-by-issuer guarantor map are not supplied. The Diabetes Health sale for 235.0 million in cash, expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, would change the debt picture but is not closed. The goodwill impairments of 328,987 thousand are non-cash and are excluded from Adjusted EBITDA, but they signal weaker projected cash flows in two reporting units.

fields.value: Principal debt at 2026-09-30 was 1,894,969 thousand against 1,750,000 thousand at 2025-12-31, an increase of 144,969 thousand. The term loans rose by 332,969 thousand (647,969 less 315,000) and the revolver by 147,000 thousand, while senior unsecured notes fell by 335,000 thousand (1,435,000 less 1,100,000, being the 10.0 million January 2026 repurchase and the 325.0 million August 2026 redemption of the 6.125% notes). Cash flows in the period also funded 127,422 thousand of acquisitions and an expanded equipment programme. Net of cash, principal debt rose by 170,418 thousand. Over the same nine months Adjusted EBITDA on the recast perimeter was 4.23% lower than a year earlier. The direction of trailing leverage is nonetheless clear. Trailing twelve months Adjusted EBITDA on the recast perimeter at 2026-09-30 equals recast FY2025 plus nine months 2026 less nine months 2025, which is recast FY2025 less 16,717 thousand (378,462 less 395,179), so the denominator is lower than at year-end while principal debt is higher; the ratio has risen. Its size cannot be built, because the 10-K annual Adjusted EBITDA includes Diabetes Health and the recast annual figure is not supplied. The only like-for-like ratio is on forward guidance: principal debt of 1,894,969 thousand against the 2026 guidance range of 510 million to 525 million gives 3.61 to 3.72 times gross, an indicative figure that rests on a management claim and ignores the 235.0 million of Diabetes Health sale proceeds, which are not yet received.

fields.value: For nine months 2026, Adjusted EBITDA of 378,462 thousand against interest expense, net of 80,403 thousand is 4.71 times. On cash interest paid of 96,639 thousand the cover is 3.92 times, against 4.12 times for nine months 2025. This is not the covenant definition, which is not supplied. The Q3 2026 interest expense of 28,600 thousand was 12.69% above Q3 2025 even though the nine-month figure was slightly lower, consistent with a larger drawn balance after April 2026. Cash interest paid for nine months 2026 (96,639) exceeded interest expense, net (80,403); accrued interest fell from 28,447 to 6,790 (page:38), which is consistent with settlement of accrued coupons, though the filing does not itself give this reason. The rate on the term loans is 5.06%, below the 6.125% coupon of the notes they replaced (which alone does not give an interest saving number, because the revolver and the first term loan also changed).

fields.value: Operating cash flow was 5.49% lower for nine months 2026 than for nine months 2025 despite revenue growth. Purchases of equipment rose from 278,492 to 392,981 thousand; the filing links this to patient equipment for capitated contracts (page:92). Patient equipment depreciation was 308,050 thousand of the 332,483 thousand continuing-operations depreciation and amortization (page:32, page:74-76), so Adjusted EBITDA, which excludes this recurring replacement-type cost, flatters cash earnings; on a continuing basis, Adjusted EBITDA less equipment purchases was negative 6,796 thousand for nine months 2026 against positive 123,716 thousand for nine months 2025. The 2026 free cash flow of 2,632 thousand and the nine-month acquisitions of 127,422 thousand were funded by borrowing. Add-backs outside goodwill, gains and equity compensation (restructuring, litigation and other non-recurring) were 21,655 thousand for nine months 2026, or 5.72% of Adjusted EBITDA, against 20,439 thousand, or 5.17%, in nine months 2025. The company's 2026 free cash flow guidance of 50 million to 75 million implies a fourth quarter of 47,368 to 72,368 thousand against a reported nine-month figure of 2,632 thousand; that is arithmetic on guidance, not a forecast.

Counting 91 days back gives 2029-05-02 and 2029-11-30 (derived). The wording does not say whether the 150.0 million test applies to each series or to both together. With 1,100,000 thousand of notes outstanding, the effective maturity of 794,969 thousand of senior secured term loans and revolver is therefore the 2029 date unless the notes are refinanced first. It answers which transaction, business, ownership and operating facts matter most to a creditor, covering transaction and ownership structure, the business and operating model, and credit-relevant history or change. Each material conclusion runs from evidence to risk mechanic to credit implication. Every fact row carries exactly one category: Documentary Fact (the cited source states it), Management Language (management's characterisation, quoted and not adopted), Analyst Interpretation (a reading of cited evidence) or Insufficient Information (the evidence is missing, and the missing datapoint is named). This pack gives no peer ranking, no instrument recommendation and no recovery conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: AdaptHealth is a national provider of home medical equipment, supplies and related services, operating three reportable segments after the pending sale of its Diabetes Health business. It is a holding company that depends on its operating subsidiaries for cash. The most important business change for a creditor is the move from fee-for-product and fixed monthly rental revenue toward at-risk capitated revenue, in which the company is paid a fixed monthly fee per member and bears the cost of the members' care. That change is driving revenue growth, equipment spending and a margin decline, and the same contract set is the main source of near-term operating uncertainty. The transactions that matter are the pending 235.0 million sale of Diabetes Health to RGH Enterprises, LLC under an agreement dated 2026-07-19, the 2026-07-29 contribution of the eCommerce subsidiary to a joint venture, the April 2026 refinancing and the August 2026 redemption of the 6.125% notes. The documents behind the sale, the joint venture and the refinancing are not in the sources, so what they permit cannot be assessed; only the filing descriptions are available. No sponsor is named in the context, and the filings show two minority holders rather than a controlling owner. Documented issuer behaviour since 2024 includes voluntary term loan repayments and no dividends or buybacks, but 2026 debt rose to fund growth and acquisitions. The reading is Neutral or Mixed on the evidence, with legal capacity for distributions and asset transfers not assessable without the credit documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The one transaction that changes the credit is the pending sale of the Diabetes Health business under an asset purchase agreement dated 2026-07-19 between the company and RGH Enterprises, LLC for 235.0 million in cash, subject to customary purchase price adjustments (Q3 10-Q page:27, page:59, page:96). It is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, subject to certain regulatory approvals and customary conditions; the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period has expired. The status is signed and pending, not closed. The business is already reported as discontinued operations, and its goodwill and intangibles are carried as assets held for sale. The filings do not say how the proceeds will be used. The credit agreement requires mandatory prepayments in connection with certain dispositions of assets to the extent proceeds are not reinvested (Q3 10-Q page:41-42), and the notes may require an offer to purchase upon the sale of certain assets (page:42), but whether either applies to this sale is not stated, and the agreement and indentures are not in the sources. Use of proceeds, any price adjustment and any transition services remain Insufficient Information. A second portfolio move, the eCommerce contribution to a joint venture on 2026-07-29, is closed; the company holds a minority interest carried at 42.5 million and the filing says the transaction is not a strategic shift (page:16-17).

It gives the fundamental credit view from the source readiness, financial base and business context handoffs, using the Q3 2026 10-Q only to test two balance sheet figures. It gives no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: AdaptHealth's fundamental credit view is cautious: a large, cash-generative home-care provider whose earnings and free cash flow are weakening while its debt is rising. The strongest support is scale and recurring revenue, with USD 395,613 thousand of operating cash flow for nine months 2026, USD 349,387 thousand of liquidity at 2026-09-30, a refinancing that leaves no notes maturing before 2029, and no dividends or buybacks. The weakest point is cash conversion: patient equipment spending of USD 392,981 thousand absorbed nearly all operating cash flow, Adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 17.5% from 20.0%, and the new capitated contracts put cost-of-care risk on the company. Three things decide the outcome: whether capitated contract margins keep recovering, how the USD 235.0 million Diabetes Health sale proceeds are used, and whether the 2029 and 2030 notes are refinanced before the secured facilities spring forward.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: AdaptHealth earned less per dollar of revenue in 2026 even as revenue grew. Revenue for nine months 2026 was USD 2,165,828 thousand, up 9.72%, but Adjusted EBITDA was USD 378,462 thousand, down 4.23%, and the margin fell by 2.5 points to 17.5%. The decline sits in Sleep Health and Wellness at Home, whose margins fell, while Respiratory Health improved. The mechanism is a rapid ramp of capitated contracts, which carried start-up labour cost and a supplier price increase before volumes settled; margin recovered in each quarter of 2026 but remains below Q3 2025 [Financial base, Business context].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation is the weakest link. Free cash flow was USD 2,632 thousand for nine months 2026, against USD 140,095 thousand a year earlier, because equipment purchases rose to USD 392,981 thousand to serve capitated members. On a continuing basis Adjusted EBITDA less equipment purchases was negative USD 6,796 thousand, against positive USD 123,716 thousand a year earlier. Acquisitions of USD 127,422 thousand and tax receivable agreement payments of USD 26,846 thousand were funded by borrowing, which is how principal debt rose to USD 1,894,969 thousand from USD 1,750,000 thousand [Financial base].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage has risen in direction but cannot be measured on one perimeter. Trailing Adjusted EBITDA on the current business equals recast FY2025 less USD 16,717 thousand, while debt is higher, so the ratio is higher than at year-end 2025. No recast FY2025 figure exists in the sources. On management guidance, principal debt is 3.66x the midpoint of USD 517.5 million of guided Adjusted EBITDA, an indicative figure that treats a forecast as given [Financial base].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and maturities are sound in the near term. Cash was USD 80,687 thousand and undrawn revolver availability USD 268.7 million, for USD 349,387 thousand. Scheduled repayments are USD 4.0 million in the rest of 2026 and USD 16.0 million in 2027. The 6.125% notes were redeemed in August 2026. The 4.625% notes of USD 500.0 million fall due on 2029-08-01 and the 5.125% notes of USD 600.0 million on 2030-03-01, and the USD 794,969 thousand of term loans and revolver spring to about 2029-05-02 if more than USD 150.0 million of the notes remains outstanding then [Financial base].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cover is adequate but lower. Adjusted EBITDA was 3.92x cash interest paid for nine months 2026 against 4.12x for nine months 2025. Covenant tests exist on total leverage and interest coverage, the company reports compliance at 2026-09-30, and the levels are not supplied, so headroom is not measurable [Source readiness, Financial base].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is shifting toward at-risk capitated revenue. It was 13.3% of nine-month 2026 revenue against 4.8%, and under these contracts the company bears members' care cost. The counterparty, term and price of the main contract are not disclosed, so concentration cannot be sized. Management claims a sequential improvement in contract profitability in Q3 2026 and offers no contract profit to test it [Business context].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Portfolio change and claims outside debt add outcomes that are not yet resolved. The sale of Diabetes Health for USD 235.0 million in cash is signed but not closed, and use of proceeds is not stated. The eCommerce subsidiary moved into a joint venture for a minority stake. Claims outside the debt figure include the tax receivable agreement liability of USD 238.9 million, operating leases of USD 126,716 thousand, finance leases of USD 39,357 thousand, two federal civil investigative demands, an unquantified cybersecurity incident and a consumer class settlement with USD 14.1 million remaining liability [Financial base, Business context].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Scale and diversification of referral sources: the company serves about 4.8 million patients a year through about 660 locations in 48 states, with fixed monthly equipment reimbursements and product resupply forming most revenue [Documentary Fact; Business context]. Operating cash flow is large: USD 395,613 thousand for nine months 2026, against USD 418,587 thousand a year earlier, which still funds a substantial equipment programme [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Liquidity and structure: USD 349,387 thousand of liquidity, a revolver running to April 2031 subject to the springing maturity, and no notes due before 2029 [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Shareholder behaviour: no dividends or buybacks, voluntary term loan repayments of USD 218.8 million in 2025, and no controlling sponsor shown among holders near 10% and 8% [Documentary Fact; Business context]. Recovery of margin through 2026: the Adjusted EBITDA margin rose from 15.4% in Q1 2026 (derived) to 17.8% in Q2 and 19.0% in Q3 [Documentary Fact; Financial base].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Margin and earnings quality: nine-month margin down to 17.5% from 20.0%, with "other non-recurring" add-backs recurring in both years at USD 15,085 thousand and USD 20,439 thousand [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Thin free cash flow after equipment spending, with growth funded by debt [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Rising debt: principal debt up USD 144,969 thousand and net principal debt up USD 170,418 thousand since year-end 2025 [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Cost-of-care risk and concentration in a small set of capitated contracts whose terms are undisclosed [Documentary Fact for the share, Insufficient Information for the terms; Business context]. Goodwill impairments of USD 328,987 thousand in nine months 2026 and a Sleep Health reporting unit within 20% of carrying value, which signal weaker projected cash flows in two reporting units and a risk of more [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Goodwill of USD 2,158,313 thousand is 51.38% of total assets and exceeds total equity, so tangible equity is negative and balance sheet asset quality offers less comfort [Analyst Interpretation; Calculations]. Unquantified claims: investigations, the cybersecurity incident and a supplier bed recall [Documentary Fact; Business context]. Management continuity: a change of Chief Financial Officer between the Q2 and Q3 2026 reports and an unreconciled restructuring savings figure [Documentary Fact; Business context].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The source readiness handoff recorded no covenant levels, no executed credit documents, no recast FY2025 and an unresolved issuer and guarantor map. The financial base handoff added that continuing-only cash flow is not supplied and that the springing maturity wording is ambiguous. The business context handoff judged this synthesis Ready with limitations, so confidence stays below High. These are restated once in Gaps and not repeated as findings.

fields.value: The evidence trace holds. Each material claim in the financial base, business context and credit synthesis handoffs was matched to a located source span or to a recomputation from located figures, and the three handoffs agree on every shared figure, period and perimeter label. The credit view of the synthesis, cautious with Medium confidence, follows from the cited basis and is not overstated. Two claims are only partly supported, both as wording rather than figures: that acquisitions and tax receivable agreement payments were funded by borrowing, which the sources support arithmetically but do not state, and operating cash flow and free cash flow quoted in the synthesis without the label that they include discontinued operations. No claim is unsupported and no contradiction between modules was found. The integrity verdict for the evaluated set is nonetheless Restricted, not Committee Ready, because the conclusions that matter most for a creditor, namely covenant headroom, structural priority and trailing leverage on the current business, rest on documents and a recast annual base that are not in the sources. The review itself is limited: it was done in the same session as the analysis, from the same extraction text, and the page locators are extraction chunks rather than printed pages.

fields.value: The strongest evidence against the cautious view is that operating cash flow remains large at 395,613 for nine months 2026, the quarterly Adjusted EBITDA margin rose each quarter of 2026 to 19.0%, management says the capitated contract is at run-rate, and the pending sale for 235.0 million equals about 12.4% of principal debt. If equipment spending is growth spending that falls after the ramp, free cash flow would recover quickly. What would make that case win: a fourth quarter free cash flow inside management's guidance (implying 47,368 to 72,368), a Diabetes Health closing in the first quarter of 2027 with proceeds applied to debt, and a margin at or above Q3 2026 in the following quarters. Downside chain with observable triggers: higher utilisation or labour cost in the capitated contract (first break: contract margin) leads to lower Adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow (transmission), then revolver drawings above the 137.0 million outstanding in October 2026 and less liquidity than 349,387, then a harder refinancing of the 2029 notes before the springing date of about 2029-05-02. Triggers to watch: quarterly margin, revolver balance, sale closing, covenant certificates when obtainable.
